chief_complaint: retrosternal burning after eating, sour reflux taste
hpi_details: A 26-year-old female presents with several weeks of retrosternal burning after eating and a sour reflux taste, worse when lying down at night. No dysphagia, weight loss, or vomiting blood.
ideas: She thinks the burning sensation in her chest is an allergic reaction to spicy foods combined with drinking too much coffee at work.
concerns: She is worried that the severe burning pain might be a bleeding ulcer eroding a hole through her stomach wall.
expectations: She hopes to get a prescription for a strong stomach medication that will stop the burning so she can finally sleep flat through the night.

core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of GERD (heartburn) is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes lifestyle modification (elevating the head of the bed, avoiding late meals) plus an empiric PPI trial, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: retrosternal burning after eating, sour reflux taste

Key HPI features: A 26-year-old female presents with several weeks of retrosternal burning after eating and a sour reflux taste, worse lying down at night. No dysphagia, weight loss, or vomiting blood.
Objective/Exam findings: Vital signs stable; abdominal exam soft and non-tender, no epigastric tenderness or signs of GI bleeding.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out GERD (heartburn).
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Cardiac chest pain without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Dysphagia.
management_principles: Elevate the head of the bed, avoid late/large meals and trigger foods, and start an empiric 8-week trial of once-daily PPI (omeprazole 20mg)
Refer for upper endoscopy if alarm features (dysphagia, weight loss, GI bleeding) are present or symptoms persist despite an adequate PPI trial
Counsel patient on trigger avoidance and the long-term risks of untreated reflux if lifestyle changes and medication are not followed
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

must_ask.say: Any sour taste in your mouth?
How long has this been going on?

history.answer: For the past few weeks, I've had a burning feeling behind my chest after eating, and sour fluid keeps coming up my throat.
It's a burning, fiery sensation right in the middle of my chest, not really a dull ache or bloating.
It is right behind my breastbone, and sometimes it travels up toward my throat, but it doesn't spread to my back or arms.
It started about three weeks ago, and it seems to be happening more frequently and getting slightly worse.
It usually flares up about thirty minutes to an hour after I finish eating, especially after large meals.
Yes, I frequently get a bitter, sour taste in the back of my mouth after eating.
Yes, it wakes me up at night feeling like hot acid is creeping up into my throat.
It definitely gets much worse whenever I lie down flat or bend over.
No, I can finish my normal meal portions without feeling full prematurely.
No, food and liquids go down smoothly without any pain or sticking sensation.
My appetite has been completely normal, and my weight has remained steady.
No, I haven't thrown up any blood or coffee-ground material, and my stools are normal brown.
I haven't been throwing up or feeling nauseated, just that sour fluid backing up.
No, I haven't felt dizzy, lightheaded, or unusually tired.
No, I've never experienced severe pain attacks in my upper right abdomen after fatty foods.
No, walking, climbing stairs, or exercising doesn't bring on the burning or make it worse.
No, I do not take painkillers like ibuprofen, naproxen, or aspirin.
I drink two cups of coffee daily and sometimes eat late-night snacks right before bed, which seems to trigger it.
I've never had an endoscopy done before, and I've never been treated for stomach bacteria.
I think my stomach is just reacting badly to spicy takeout and drinking three cups of coffee at work every morning.
The pain can be so sharp when I lie down that I'm terrified I have a bleeding ulcer eating through my stomach.
I don't have any chronic medical conditions or health problems.
I have never had any surgeries, and I've never been admitted to a hospital.
I'm not taking any prescription medications, over-the-counter drugs, or vitamins.
I don't have any known allergies to medications.
No, I have never smoked cigarettes.
I only have a glass of wine or beer socially on weekends.
I work as an office administrator and live with a roommate in an apartment.
My parents are both healthy, with no family history of stomach cancer, ulcer disease, or heart conditions.
My last period was two weeks ago, my cycles are regular, and there is no possibility of pregnancy.

exam.finding: The patient looks comfortable, well-nourished, and in no acute distress.
Blood pressure 118/76 mmHg, heart rate 72 beats/min, respiratory rate 14 breaths/min, body temperature 36.6°C, oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Conjunctivae are pink without pallor; sclerae are anicteric.
No palpable cervical or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy, including Virchow node.
No chest wall tenderness on palpation; no visible chest deformity.
Regular rate and rhythm with normal S1 and S2; no murmurs, gallops, or friction rubs.
Clear breath sounds bilaterally without wheezes, crackles, or rhonchi.
Abdomen is flat and symmetric with no surgical scars or visible distension.
Normoactive bowel sounds present in all four quadrants; no vascular bruits.
Abdomen is soft and non-tender throughout; no epigastric tenderness, rigidity, or palpable masses.
Negative Murphy sign; no tenderness or inspiratory arrest on right upper quadrant palpation.
No rebound tenderness or involuntary guarding anywhere in the abdomen.
